_about: Perf Tuner catalog. Every entry is a change the picture does not show: no resolution, quality level, upscaler, frame cap, LOD or mip bias can appear here; the tuner refuses the file if one does. Engine defaults quoted are Unreal 5.6.1's, read from the engine source; the game's own values are from its cooked DefaultEngine.ini and DefaultScalability.ini. Edit with the game closed.

tweaks.title: Texture pool
tweaks.what: Gives the texture streamer a pool sized to the card, a quarter of its memory between 800 and 3000 MB (2700 MB on a 12 GB card), instead of the 600 MB the game's High texture setting allows (800 at Ultra). Textures then stay resident at full detail instead of being dropped and re-streamed as you turn, which is what the mip pops and the small hitches on a turn are. The picture is the same or sharper, never worse. Offered on cards with 8 GB or more; the engine's own clamp to real memory stays in force, and a bigger pool set by you or the game is kept.

tweaks.title: Nanite streaming pool
tweaks.what: Grows the memory Nanite keeps its geometry pages in from the 512 MB the game set ('decreasing VRAM' in its config) to a sixteenth of the card's memory, 512 to 1024 MB (768 MB on a 12 GB card). In dense areas the pages stop cycling in and out as you move, so fewer detail pops and less streaming work each frame. Geometry drawn is the same.

tweaks.title: No forced purge on level unload
tweaks.what: When a streamed level unloads (the game's seamless dungeon loading does this), the engine by default forces a full garbage collection at once, which its own help text calls 'at the expense of a hitch'. Off, the memory is reclaimed by the next regular purge instead. Nothing on screen changes; the hitch at a dungeon boundary goes.

tweaks.title: Garbage collection pacing
tweaks.what: Runs the engine's object purge every 120 seconds instead of every 61. Each purge is a short pause on the game thread; half as many of them. The pass itself takes a little longer because more has piled up, and nothing on screen changes. This spaces hitches out rather than raising the frame rate, so the measurement will read 'no change'.

tweaks.title: Nanite shadows on the compute queue
tweaks.what: Lets Nanite rasterize its shadow depths on the GPU's compute queue, overlapping other work, the way its main rasterization already does. Engine default is off. Same shadows, same geometry; whether it gains anything depends on the card and driver, so measure it. Measured on an RTX 3060 under Proton: no change (6 Oct 2026).

tweaks.title: Nanite without mesh shaders
tweaks.what: Makes Nanite's hardware rasterizer use plain vertex shaders instead of mesh shaders. On Windows mesh shaders are the faster path; under Proton they go through VKD3D's mesh-shader translation, where NVIDIA has had both slowdowns and glitches. The picture is identical either way. Measure it; keep whichever is faster. Measured on an RTX 3060 under GE-Proton 11-7: 3.4% less frame time, consistent over both rounds (6 Oct 2026).

tweaks.title: Reflex off
tweaks.what: Turns NVIDIA Reflex off. Reflex trims input lag by holding the CPU back so the GPU never has a queue of frames waiting; that same hold can cost a few frames per second. Picture unchanged. Measure it: if you see no gain, leave Reflex on, the lower lag is worth more. Measured on an RTX 3060 under Proton: no change (6 Oct 2026), so Reflex stayed on.
